transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-22
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Clarke (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (NexaHealth - Head of ML), Samira Ortiz (NexaHealth - Infra Lead), Daniel Park (NexaHealth - Security)

Auto-summary: Quick onboarding sync. VPC peering in progress, credentials provided but testing failed due to subnet routing. Benchmarks show preliminary latencies ~120ms p50 on hosted model; costs higher than expected at current q4 quantization setting. Decided to run canary Friday and exchange more security docs.

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, jump in if you need to. Quick agenda — access status, benchmark peek, next steps for canary.

[00:22] Jordan: Thanks, Avery. Quick status — we gave Samira the account details, she tried peering, hit an issue, anyway will ping the logs.

[00:35] Samira: yeah, so we attempted the VPC peering this morning, the route tables weren't propagating to the private subnet, uh, looks like a small routing rule missing on our side.

[01:05] Priya: Ok that matches what we saw — when we try to run the pilot we can't reach the runtime endpoint from your subnets, error looked like connection refused then timeouts. Could be security group or NACL.

[01:33] Daniel: From security side, we also want to confirm KMS integration — where are keys stored with Redwood, can we bring our own KMS? Also audit logs retention, is there an option for 13 months?

[02:05] Avery: Yes, standard — we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated options; we'll share the KMS integration doc. Audit logs default retention is 90 days but enterprise can opt in for longer retention as an add-on. I'll send the SOC 2 excerpt as well.

[03:10] Jordan: Cool. On the benchmarks we ran your sample prompts across our dev set — attached spreadsheet in the drive link you sent — p50 around 120ms for shorter prompts, tails up to 400ms for long context. Cost estimate came back a bit higher than we expected.

[03:40] Priya: Right, that was on the baseline quantization (q4) setting and no prefix caching. If you enable prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes and try q3ab quantization, we often see 20-30% lower latency and cost drop, but occasionally quality diffs — we can run a quick A/B.

[04:05] Jordan: Quality is critical for us; we can't tolerate hallucinations even if cost savings are good.

[04:20] Priya: Understood, we'll keep the eval set fixed, run q3ab vs q4 and share top-level metrics: ROUGE-ish / exact match on intent, plus token-level cost.

[05:00] Samira: For the canary — our infra window on Friday is 10:00-14:00 PST — can Redwood schedule a short canary during that? We'll need a test VPC peering established by then.

[05:25] Avery: Yes Friday works. Priya, can you own the canary run?

[05:30] Priya: Yep, I'll coordinate. We'll do a small traffic ramp to mimic production: spike to 200 rps for 5 minutes, then hold at 50 rps for 15.

[05:48] Daniel: On compliance, also want to confirm SAML SSO for admin console and RBAC for audit teams.

[06:10] Avery: SSO/SAML supported, RBAC roles include admin, viewer, devops — we'll share role mapping doc.

[07:05] Jordan: A couple of clarifying Qs — latency targets: we want p95 < 300ms for chat-like flows. Are those realistic on dedicated vs hosted?

[07:30] Priya: On Dedicated with pinned GPUs and optimized batching you should hit p95 < 200ms for typical 1k token workloads; hosted depends on load and multi-tenant variance — we can provide dedicated nodes for the pilot if you want deterministic latency.

[07:58] Jordan: Cost will go up for Dedicated though. We need to present to finance next week with a cost/latency tradeoff.

[08:15] Avery: We'll put together a two-column estimate: hosted vs dedicated for the pilot footprint you gave, including projected token costs and a monthly reserved cost if you want dedicated pools.

[09:05] Samira: Back to access — I attached the VPC peering screenshots in the chat, there's an error id that looks like route-prop. We'll share the logs to you.

[09:35] Priya: Great — please drop the logs to the shared folder and include the traceroute. We'll triage and send a small runbook.

[10:12] Jordan: On data residency — some of our data must remain in EU regions, is Redwood able to pin model inference to a region?

[10:35] Avery: Yes, we can route to region-specific endpoints and we have EU regions available — we'll note that in the estimate. For the pilot we can spin nodes in eu-west-1 if needed.

[11:00] Daniel: On the topic of model fallbacks — if there's capacity constraints, what's the fallback policy? We can't have sudden model behavior variance.

[11:28] Priya: We recommend model variants with controlled regression testing; for live fallback we can set a policy to only fallback to verified model variants with the same API contract and flag any quality diffs to your dashboard.

[12:10] Jordan: Great. Any blockers besides the VPC peering and KMS/SSO docs?

[12:25] Samira: We also saw an IAM role permission denied when trying to write to the S3 bucket that holds logs. Might be an assumed role issue.

[12:48] Priya: We'll send the exact assume-role policy you should add.

[13:10] Avery: Ok, let's recap — actions: Redwood sends SOC2 excerpt, KMS integration doc, SAML/SSO role mapping, and the assume-role template. Priya runs q3ab vs q4 A/B benchmarks and uploads CSV. Samira to provide VPC logs and confirm peering window. Jordan to share prompt eval sets and SLOs.

[14:00] Jordan: Sounds good. A couple of micro items — can you include a simple cost calc for token price per 1M tokens at the three quant levels?

[14:18] Avery: Yep, we'll include that in the estimate doc.

[14:30] Priya: Also note small transcription glitch from our last demo — KV cache got transcribed as KV cash in the notes, so apologies if any docs copied that.

[15:00] Samira: ha, yeah that was funny.

[15:12] (long pause while screen share and doc link shared)

[20:00] Priya: Quick technical note about tuning — for repeated prompt prefixes we can set prefix caching TTL to 24 hours for the pilot; that'll shave tails. We'll check with you on cache invalidation rules.

[25:00] Jordan: On evals, we'll run the two quant variants through our automated regression harness. If quality drops more than 1.5% on intent matching we'll reject that quant.

[30:00] Priya: Understood. We'll report per-prompt diffs and an aggregate score.

[34:15] Avery: Ok final admin — I'll send an invite for the Friday canary and include the runbook, and Priya will post the benchmark link.

[34:40] Jordan: One more security Q — do you support customer-managed HSM for extreme compliance?

[35:05] Avery: We support HSM integrations on Private deployments, yes — we'll surface that in the doc.

[35:40] Daniel: Thanks, that's useful.

[36:10] Priya: Any other blockers?

[36:25] Jordan: No, thanks team.

[36:40] Avery: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items in the next 24-48 hours.

[36:55] End of call — action items and next steps summarized in meeting notes.

References:
- Benchmark spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood.example/nexa/benchmarks.csv
- Security docs: https://redwood.example/security/soc2-excerpt.pdf
- Runbook (will be shared): /shared/runbooks/nexa-canary-runbook.md

Recap (auto): VPC peering + route table fix required; Redwood to share KMS/SOC2/SSO docs; Priya to run quant A/B and provide benchmarks; canary scheduled for Friday pending peering confirmation.
